findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Observed multiple in use sauce bottles to be missing date marking. Discussed with PIC, sauce was discarded and bottles were remade with correct dates. Ensure any item removed from its original container is date marked.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Observed multiple containers of TCS foods to be held past their 7 day maximum. Discussed with PIC, containers were pulled and discarded. Ensure all TCS foods are date marked and that staff is regularly checking dates to ensure 7 day maximum is not passed. 

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
6-301.11: Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap. 

Observed no soap in the dispenser at the hand sink near the ware washing area. Discussed with PIC. Ensure hand sinks are properly stocked at all times - soap, paper towels, hot water. PIC replaced the soap upon request. Ensure staff is aware to replace as needed. COS.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

(REPEAT) Observed the sani bucket in the kitchen area to be 0 ppm. Quat at the 3 compartment sink was 0 ppm. The quat is very low and not enough sanitizer is drawing to the dispenser at the 3 compartment sink. A shipment of quaternary ammonium is due tomorrow on the truck. Discussed with PIC. PIC has bleach to use as sanitizer in the sani buckets until tomorrow. Utilize the heated dish machine for ware washing or the 3 compartment sink may be used for the wash and rinse process, while the heated dish machine should be used for the 3rd step - sanitize. Ensure staff is aware to use test strips to verify sanitization concentration at sani buckets and the 3 compartment sink. Facility has the appropriate test strips to verify. COS. Repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 6/6/23.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
6-305.11: (A) Dressing rooms or dressing areas shall be designated if EMPLOYEES routinely change their clothes in the establishment. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be provided for the orderly storage of EMPLOYEES' clothing and other possessions. 

Observed multiple winter coats in the dry storage area on top of boxes. Cease practice. Winter coats should not be stored in the dry storage area. Winter coats should be stored in a designated employee area. Discussed with PIC. COS.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).  

Observed two trays of raw chicken above uncooked bacon and ground beef - improper storage order. Discussed with the cook. Ensure staff is aware that chicken must always be at the bottom of the storage order shelf (cross contamination concerns). Observed raw shell eggs placed over cooked bacon in the reach-in cooler. Inspector moved the eggs next to the bacon. Ensure raw shell eggs are not above ready-to-eat foods. Discussed with cook. COS.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

Observed both the kitchen and dining area sani buckets to be 0 ppm - no concentration of quaternary ammonium. Discussed with PIC. PIC indicated it had been quite a bit of time since the sani bucket had been changed out. Ensure frequent sani bucket changes in order to maintain concentration of sanitizer: 200-400 ppm for quat. Facility has test strips to verify concentration levels. Utilize test strips to verify levels of concentration. Ensure staff is aware. COS.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
4-904.11: (A) cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed to prevent FOOD- and lip-contact surface contamination. (B) UTENSILS not prewrapped shall be presented so only handles are touched by EMPLOYEES and/or CONSUMERS. (C) SINGLE-SERVCIE ARTICLES intended for FOOD- and lip-contact shall be furnished for CONSUMER with wrapper or APPROVED dispenser. 

(REPEAT) Observed plates and bowls in the dining area to be flipped upright. Ensure all dish ware is turned over so food- and lip-contact surfaces are not exposed. Cross contamination concerns for dish ware. Discussed with PIC. Ensure all dishes are flipped over (including single service items) by next routine inspection. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 1/27/23.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED. 

Observed food handler to improperly wash hands. No barrier was used to turn off the faucet handles. Discussed with employee and instructed to re-wash hands properly, followed by utilizing a barrier such as a paper towel to turn off faucet handles. Ensure staff is aware of proper hand washing technique. Discussed with employee and PIC. COS.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
3-501.18: (A) FOOD shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time criteria. If container or PACKAGE does not bear a date or day or if inappropriately marked with date or day exceeding temperature and time combination. (B) Refrigerated RTE TCS FOOD prepared in FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and dispensed through vending machine shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time. 

Observed multiple items to be expired within the walk-in cooler and reach-in cooler: marinara sauce, ham salad, diced ham (2x containers), and hot dogs. Discussed discarding food items after 7-day mark. Items were 8-10 days old. Ham salad was 20 days old. Ensure staff is routinely going through the coolers to discard outdated food. Utilize the 7-day date marking system appropriately. All mentioned items were voluntarily discarded. Discussed with PIC and employees in kitchen. COS.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
4-904.11: (A) cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed to prevent FOOD- and lip-contact surface contamination. (B) UTENSILS not prewrapped shall be presented so only handles are touched by EMPLOYEES and/or CONSUMERS. (C) SINGLE-SERVCIE ARTICLES intended for FOOD- and lip-contact shall be furnished for CONSUMER with wrapper or APPROVED dispenser. 

Observed all the plates and bowls in the dining area to be flipped upright. Ensure all dish ware is turned over so food- and lip-contact surfaces are not exposed. Cross contamination concern for dish ware. Discussed with PIC. PIC was in compliance to cease practice and begin turning over dish ware. Ensure all dishes are flipped over (including single service items) by next routine inspection.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-303.11: (A) Cleaning agents used to clean EQUIPMENT shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. (B) Chemical SANITIZERS shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. 

Observed no sanitization bucket upon start of inspection. Employee and PIC were actively prepping food. Ensure a sani bucket is prepared prior to engaging in food preparation. Ensure sani buckets have active concentration of sanitizer at all times. Facility utilizes quaternary ammonium - 200 to 400 ppm. Facility has test strips to check concentration. Discussed with PIC. New sani bucket was made - 400 ppm. COS.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-201.11: Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE. 

Observed the following areas no longer smooth and easily cleanable: 
1. Interior caulking of the hand sink in the kitchen is molded. Re-caulk the hand sink creases.
2. Dish machine (in front of spray nozzle) needs re-caulked due to black, moldy caulk from water exposure.
3. The cabinet in the kitchen (next to the fryer, top cabinet) needs repainted on the back wall inside of the cabinet. Paint is coming away. Re-seal with paint.

Discussed repairs with PIC. PIC indicated maintenance will take care of the above items. Correct by next routine inspection.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
(REPEAT SITUATION) 4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria.

On arrival, the sani bucket in the kitchen is observed at 0 ppm quat. The bottle, and previous conversations with the technician, indicate that a minimum concentration of 150 ppm is required for effectively sanitizing surfaces. After further investigation, it appears that the machine metering solution at 150 ppm. Inspector discussed with the PIC and stated that the solution is likely to run to low for effective use quickly in this situation. It is suggested that the PIC contacts the technician for service. The bucket was remade during the inspection to correct the immediate situation. Education also took place in relation to manually making the solution until proper concentrations are consistently being metered by the machine.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
4-903.12: (A) Cleaned and SANITIZED EQUIPMENT may not be stored in locker, toilet, garbage, or mechanical rooms. Also they cannot be stored under sewer lines, under leaking water lines, under open stairwells, or under other sources of contamination. 

The facility has a single drawer where employees may store personal items in the kitchen. This is a good practice! However, the probe thermometer was observed in this drawer during the inspection. Employee (and later PIC) indicated that the thermometer’s storage location is on the counter next to the oven. The thermometer was sanitized and then stored in its normal/correct location during the inspection to correct. PIC is aware that the food contact items should be stored away from personal items to prevent contamination.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. 

The bottom shelf of the cabinet to the right of the hood system is no longer smooth and easily cleanable. Measuring cups are observed stored at this location. PIC instructed to ensure that areas where food contact items are stored remain smooth and easily cleanable.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. 

In the dinning area, the section under the cabinets has a gross amount of food debris that appears to have been wet. A discussion with the PIC revealed that there was a back up in the drain behind this location recently and the food debris is likely a result of that. PIC indicated that they thought the area had been cleaned. PIC instructed to ensure that cleaning takes place as needed, and specifically is instructed to clean this location of the debris. PIC vacuumed the debris up and had the location mopped during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated
findings.comment:
3-202.15: FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants. 

Multiple cans are observed with dents. Two specifically have significant dents in the areas of the three joining seams on the can. Inspector discussed the situation and the associated concern with the PIC and the two cans were moved to the discard pile during the inspection.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria.

On arrival, the sani bucket in the kitchen is observed at 100 ppm quat. The bottle, and previous conversations with the technician, indicate that a minimum concentration of 150 ppm is required for effectively sanitizing surfaces. After further investigation, it appears that the machine metering solution at 150 ppm. Inspector discussed with the PIC and stated that the solution is likely to run to low for effective use quickly in this situation. It is suggested that the PIC contacts the technician for service. The bucket was remade during the inspection to correct the immediate situation.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-201.17: (A) Attachments to walls and ceilings (i.e. light fixtures, fans, decorative items) shall be EASILY CLEANABLE. 

The hand sink in the kitchen and the hand sink in the dish room both have open gaps at the top of the sinks that are not easily cleanable. PIC is instructed to ensure a smooth and easily cleanable surface is maintained around all sources of moister.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. 

A large accumulation of ice is observed from the walk in freezer cooling unit to floor. Multiple shelves and the floor are observed coated as well as multiple items of packaged foods. The ice accumulation was discussed with the PIC and they are instructed to clean often enough to prevent accumulation.
